markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (98%)** · Confident · Read in turn
One-class conformal set, second-model agreement, and every region leans away from invasive [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 98%, Normal 2% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | {Benign}, α=0.1 | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.998 / 86th percentile | Usable; simulated stain degradation |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Mixed neighbors, weak support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 7, 8, 9) · ↓ invasive · Strongest lower-invasive association; AI spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Small invasive-leaning association; region risk is 0% · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (region 11) · ↓ invasive · Present; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Validated
- **Nuclear pleomorphism** (region 0) · ↑ invasive · Scored below typical here, pulling away from invasive · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deleting its top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier; normal lobules is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Stain degradation (severity 3, simulated) shifts features despite the high reliability score.
- Calibration was tested on 132 cases only; ECE CI reaches 0.18, so 98% may overstate.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 7, 8, 9**: confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; this concept failed its AI spot check.
2. **Region 3**: look for tumor infiltrating stroma, this concept's top-scoring region.
3. **Region 0**: assess nuclear pleomorphism; similar in-situ case BACH_0043 scored higher there.
